standard_prerequisites.name: n-connected pointed types
standard_prerequisites.statement: A pointed type (A,a_0) is n-connected if the map a_0 : unit -> A is n-connected, i.e. if trunc n (fiber of a_0 at a) is contractible for all a.
standard_prerequisites.use: The hypotheses of the statement are that (A,a_0) is n-connected and (B,b_0) is m-connected, and the proof uses exactly this by viewing a_0 and b_0 as maps out of the unit.

standard_prerequisites.name: Induction principle for connected maps
standard_prerequisites.statement: If f : A -> B is n-connected and P : B -> type is a family of n-types, then a section of P o f extends to a section of P.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is applied twice, once at source line 1619 to the map a_0 : unit -> A and once at source line 1623 to b_0 : unit -> B.

standard_prerequisites.name: Fibers and truncation levels of function types
standard_prerequisites.statement: The fiber of precomposition with b_0 over f(a) is the type Sigma k : (prd b:B P(a,b)), f(a) = k(b_0).
standard_prerequisites.use: It identifies the type Q(a) with that fiber at source lines 1620-1622.

core_obligations: Define Q(a) := Sigma k : (prd b:B P(a,b)), (f(a) = k(b_0)) and observe that (g,p) inhabits Q(a_0) (source lines 1616-1618).

Reduce the goal to showing that Q is a family of (n-1)-types: since a_0 : unit -> A is (n-1)-connected, the induction principle for connected maps then produces ell with ell(a_0) = (g,p), and h(a,b) := proj1(ell(a))(b) has the required type (source line 1619).
Identify Q(a) with the fiber over f(a) of the precomposition map (prd b:B P(a,b)) -> P(a,b_0) along b_0 (source lines 1620-1622).

Apply the same induction principle to the (m-1)-connected map b_0 : unit -> B: it suffices that each P(a,b) be an (n+m)-type, which is the hypothesis, to conclude that the fiber is (n-1)-truncated; this is the step that forces the level n+m in the statement (source line 1623).
Read off the homotopies q and r and the coherence p = opp(q(a_0)) `ct` r(b_0) from the equality ell(a_0) = (g,p) (source lines 1605-1613).

proof_roadmap.step: Introduce the auxiliary family Q and its element at a_0.
Reduce the existence of h to the truncation level of Q, using connectedness of a_0.
Recognise Q(a) as a fiber of precomposition and bound its truncation level by the induction principle for the m-connected map b_0.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 8.6.2 at source lines 1600-1614, the wedge connectivity lemma: for pointed types (A,a_0) n-connected and (B,b_0) m-connected and a family P : A -> B -> type of (n+m)-types, sections f of P(-,b_0) and g of P(a_0,-) agreeing at the basepoints extend to a section h of P, with specified homotopies satisfying p = opp(q(a_0)) `ct` r(b_0). The proof (source lines 1615-1624) is not a direct application of one induction principle: it first manufactures the auxiliary family Q(a) := Sigma k, f(a) = k(b_0) together with its element (g,p) at a_0 (lines 1616-1618), then applies the induction principle for the (n-1)-connected map a_0 to reduce to a truncation-level statement about Q (line 1619), then identifies Q(a) with a fiber of precomposition along b_0 (lines 1620-1622) and invokes the same principle a second time for the (m-1)-connected map b_0, at which point the level arithmetic n+m is what makes the two applications mesh (line 1623). The two connectedness hypotheses are used at two different stages and on two different maps.
